source.title: How Few-shot Demonstrations Affect Prompt-based Defenses Against LLM Jailbreak Attacks
source.authors: Yan-Shu Wang; Shuaishuai Yang; Jingjing He; Tong Yang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates a forced-affirmative prefix attack and reports its effect on harmful-request safety, a different evaluation method from fine-tuning or measuring tokenwise KL. Its few-shot defense experiments are in-context prompting, not fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: The paper's few-shot experiments add demonstrations to system prompts without updating model parameters, so they do not test harmful or benign fine-tuning (V1–V2). It does not measure aligned-versus-base KL by response position, safety-related parameters or ranks, causes of first-token concentration, or methods for deepening safety (V3, V5–V7). The Prefix Rejection result is the directly relevant test of a compliant/affirmative opening for V4. The other recorded results concern in-context demonstrations interacting with prompt defenses; these are relevant to the broader safety subject but do not measure any listed version as worded, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited findings from other work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study's main topic, few-shot demonstrations interacting with prompt defenses, matches no version. Only one incidental result bears on V4: Table 6 reports Pangu-Embedded-7B's safe rate under a 'Prefix Rejection (forced affirmative)' attack. That attack is an instructed prefix injection in the user prompt, not a true prefill of response tokens. It is a weak, single-model test of V4 in a new setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that few-shot demonstrations enhance RoP (up to about +4.3–4.5%) and degrade ToP (up to -21.2%), and that think-mode models are more vulnerable to jailbreaks and degrade with few-shot under both prompts. They recommend RoP with few-shot (preferably FS-Harmful) and avoiding ToP with few-shot. Note that the abstract says 'up to 4.5%' while the introduction and conclusion say 4.3%.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates in-context prompt demonstrations and jailbreak attacks, not fine-tuning, tokenwise KL measurement, weight localization, or safety-deepening training.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary by model, defense prompt type, demonstration type, and benchmark. Think-mode results are often more negative; Table 13 also reports ToP+FS improving over ToP for Qwen3-8B on HarmBench.

fits_no_version.finding: Few-shot in-context demonstrations change safe rate under jailbreaks differently with role-oriented and task-oriented system prompts. The effect is mostly positive with RoP and mostly negative with ToP, and negative for think-mode models; it varies by model and dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context demonstrations interact with prompt-based defenses: they reinforce role prompts and dilute task prompts. This is not evidence about fine-tuning.

record.problems: The authors state that the proposed mechanisms are hypotheses and that attention visualization or probing would provide stronger confirmation. They used three demonstrations and primarily evaluated 7–8B models. Reported values are not fully consistent across sections: Table 11 gives negative aggregate RoP means while the text describes positive averages; Table 12 and Table 8 differ slightly for some AdvBench entries. Some Table 13 few-shot variants are not specified.
record.rows_left_out: None of the listed, claim-relevant numerical interaction results were left out; 55 rows are included.

untested.parts: True prefilling of the assistant's response, adversarial suffixes (e.g. GCG) and decoding changes are not tested. Prefix Rejection results are broken out by attack type only for Pangu-Embedded-7B, so no per-model breakdown exists for the other models.
No fine-tuning on harmful data is done. Demonstrations are in-context refusals only.
No benign fine-tuning is done. Benign Q&A appears only as in-context demonstrations.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models is measured.
No weight or rank localization is done.
The paper does not study causes of shallowness. Its mechanisms concern prompt attention and in-context learning.

missing.what: Pangu-Embedded-7B safe rates under the other attacks give context for Prefix Rejection: AIM 72.1%, Refusal Suppression 85.6%, DAN 89.2%. Prefix Rejection is the strongest attack.

record.verdict_notes: The V4 link is borderline: Prefix Rejection asks the model to start affirmatively rather than prefilling its output, so it tests a weaker form of 'getting past the opening'. The judge is Qwen3Guard-Gen-8B. There is no tokenwise analysis. Neither original source is this paper.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful examples are used as in-context refusals, not for fine-tuning; the study does not test fine-tuning on harmful examples.
Benign examples are used in prompts, not for fine-tuning; the study does not test ordinary or carefully selected benign fine-tuning data.
No per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models is measured.
The paper tests a forced-affirmative Prefix Rejection attack, but not suffixes, decoding changes, or a general intervention that merely prefills a compliant opening.
No weights or ranks are localized, edited, or ablated.
The proposed mechanisms concern prompt interactions, not the data or training objective producing shallow safety.
No training intervention spreads safety beyond the first response tokens or tests whether deepened safety holds up.

rows.subject: Pangu-Embedded-7B
rows.operation_detail: Apply the Prefix Rejection forced-affirmative jailbreak attack.
rows.note: The attack lowers safety, but the reported safe rate remains 63.1%; the result is a partial rather than near-total loss of safety.
rows.check: The link and state are acceptable. The condition should say the attack is an instruction-based prefix injection (citing Wei et al.), not a prefilled assistant response. Safe rate falls from 99.8% to 63.1%, so refusal is substantially but not fully defeated.

relationships.condition: Pangu-Embedded-7B, AdvBench, no defense, instructed forced-affirmative prefix (Prefix Rejection)
relationships.reason: r1: safe rate drops from 99.8% to 63.1%. This is the most effective of six attacks, but most requests are still refused, so the instructed affirmative opening does not reliably defeat refusal.
relationships.display_finding: The safe rate drops from 99.8% to 63.1%, the largest drop among six attacks, yet most requests are still refused.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.reason: The forced-affirmative attack reduces safe rate from 99.8% to 63.1%, showing an effect but not near-total safety loss; this is row r1.
